data.name: Archibald
data.gender_notes: Archibald is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Archibald is derived from the Greek words archein, meaning 'to rule', and baldos, meaning 'strong'. This name was given to those who ruled over their people with strength and wisdom. In the Middle Ages, Archibald was a popular name for Scottish and Irish rulers. The name Archibald carries the meaning “Ruler of the true people” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Archibald usually hope their child will grow to embody ruler of the true people and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_latin.name: Archibaldus
in_latin.meaning: Exaltare, magnificare, honorare, regnare, dominare, triumphare
in_latin.long_meaning: Archibaldus, nomen sapientis et fortis viri. Exaltare et magnificare, honorare et regnare, dominare et triumphare sunt virtutes quae virum fortem et sapientem faciunt. Exaltare significat elevare et majus facere, magnificare significat laudare et glorificare, honorare significat reverentia et dignitas, regnare significat gubernare et dominare, dominare significat imperare et potestatem habere, triumphare significat victoria et gloria. Vir sapientis et fortis est qui huiusmodi virtutes habet et eos exercet.
